script.screenplayHelp: This becomes the source of truth for voices, shots, keyframes, and assembly.

sidebar.principleHelp: The script drives story, dialogue, timing, and shot choice. Characters provide faces and voices. Location sheets provide the visual world memory.
sidebar.ltxHelp: Default for short generated video shots.
sidebar.voiceHelp: The selected ElevenLabs or Irodori-TTS workflow turns dialogue into editable audio clips.
sidebar.locationSheetsHelp: Reference images for consistent spaces and angles.
sidebar.notesHelp: Voices, keyframes, and video renders are wired. Timeline assembly is the next pass.

setup.title: Make it look like a friend posted it.
setup.description: Pick the kind of post, write the hook, and tell Lumeweft what is being sold. The workflow turns that into editable dialogue, keyframes, video clips, and a timeline.
setup.templateDescription: Each one writes a full default script — shots, dialogue, and camera — as a starting point. Pick the closest, then customize the prompt on the Generate step. These are templates, not locked formats; the real ad is yours to edit.
setup.productDescription: The one thing that's in every shot.
setup.productPlaceholder: What are you selling? e.g. a can of Red Bull
setup.energyDescription: How does the person on camera feel?
setup.frameRateHelp: Locked to 25 fps — LTX 2.3's native rate for clean motion and lip-sync.
setup.detailsHelp: All optional. Leave them and the workflow fills in sensible defaults; add any to steer the result. You can also tweak every line later in Script Review.
setup.minimumHelp: Format, hook, product, and tone are all you need — fine-tune the full script on the Generate step.

references.title: Anchor the product, creator, and room.
references.description: These are optional, but UGC gets more believable when the AI has real references for the product, person, and phone-camera environment.
references.productHelp: Packaging shots, close-ups, app screens - anything that locks the product identity.
references.creator: The Creator
references.creatorHelp: Creator or avatar image with outfit, expressions, social-camera personality.
references.roomHelp: Bathroom, kitchen, desk, gym - the world the phone lives in.
references.openProjectRequired: Open or create a project before uploading a reference image.
references.pickerFailed: Could not open the image picker.
references.imagesOnly: Only image files can be used as references.
references.tip: A creator reference plus a room reference keeps the same person in the same place across shots. That continuity is what makes UGC ads feel real instead of stitched together.

preview.title: Social preview
preview.generateFirst: Generate at least one video first.
preview.tooltip: Preview the ready clips back-to-back in this phone.

why.title: Why this works
why.description: UGC ads work when they feel native to the feed. The defaults here favor handheld framing, real skin tones, clear product handling, and editable shot-by-shot control.

generate.title: Generate the whole ad in one pass.
generate.description: Seedance 2.0 takes your full prompt + the references and builds the entire ad — all the cuts, performance, and native audio — in a single clip. Pick a length, review the prompt, and generate.
generate.creator: Creator
generate.aiDescription: Copy this {{template}} template's prompt, paste it into ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini / any LLM (or your own), then paste the result into the box below. It rewrites the script for your exact product — no credits, your choice of model.
generate.seedanceTooltip: Cloud Seedance 2.0 — uses your references to lock the product and creator. The quality path.
generate.ltxTooltip: Local LTX 2.3 — composes a first frame from your references, then animates it (one continuous shot). Slower on local GPUs.
generate.modelHelp: Seedance (cloud) uses your references to lock the product and creator with true scene cuts. LTX 2.3 (local) auto-composes a first frame from your references, then animates it — one continuous shot, kept on your own GPU. (No references? LTX falls back to prompt-only.)
generate.readyPrefix: Your ad is ready — hit play in the
generate.readySuffix: to watch it. Saved to your project assets too; drag it onto the timeline to edit or export. Not happy? Tweak the prompt and generate again.

gettingStarted.title: Get from install to first generation
gettingStarted.intro: Velorn can run local, cloud, and hybrid AI workflows. This guide keeps the first-run path simple: choose how you want to connect, prepare the workflows you need, then start creating.
gettingStarted.choosePathHelp: Use Quick Start if you want Velorn to guide you through a starter kit. Use Bring Your Own ComfyUI if you already have a custom ComfyUI install and just need Velorn pointed at it.

steps.projectsHelp: Pick where projects and generated media live.
steps.connectionHelp: Connect to local ComfyUI or use cloud workflows.
steps.workflowHelp: Open starter kits to prepare models and nodes by use case.
steps.generateReady: Local or cloud generation is available.
steps.generateHelp: Connect local ComfyUI or add a cloud API key.

workspace.title: Workspace folder
workspace.description: Projects, imported assets, and generated media live under your selected projects folder.
workspace.none: No default projects folder selected yet.

connection.title: Local ComfyUI connection
connection.description: Velorn talks to a local ComfyUI server on localhost only. If generations fail immediately, check the saved port first.
connection.portHelp: If your ComfyUI window uses a different port, update it in Settings before generating.

workflow.title: Workflow requirements
workflow.description: Each workflow can require custom nodes, models, or a partner API key even though the workflow file is already bundled in the app.
workflow.help1: Open Settings > Workflow Setup to scan every built-in workflow at once.
workflow.help2: Use Generate for workflow-specific fallback tools such as Load in ComfyUI and per-workflow Re-check.
workflow.help3: This is the fastest way to find why a workflow works on one machine but not another.

cloud.title: Cloud Workflows API key
cloud.description: One Comfy.org key unlocks the {{count}} cloud-rendered starter workflows: Grok, Kling, Vidu, Nano Banana, and Seedream.
cloud.ready: Cloud-powered workflows are ready to go.
cloud.detail: Paste your key once and you can skip local GPU setup for these workflows.
cloud.help1: Great for low-VRAM machines — cloud workflows run on Comfy.org and cost a few cents per generation.
cloud.help2: You can skip this and come back any time.

stock.title: Stock setup
stock.description: The Stock tab uses Pexels. Add a key once and you can browse and import footage or photos directly into the project.
stock.notDetected: No Pexels API key detected yet.
stock.help: You can skip this until you need stock content.

tour.intro: This quick orientation answers where to go next. Detailed editing and prompting techniques can be learned from the videos.
tour.editorDescription: This is the day-to-day editing view once media is inside the project.
tour.editor1: Assets panel: import videos, audio, and images, then drag them to the timeline.
tour.editor2: Preview: review media and send a frame to Generate as a starting keyframe.
tour.editor3: Timeline: trim, ripple, snap, markers, and arrange your cut.
tour.editor4: Inspector: transform, crop, timing, effects, text, and adjustments for the selected item.
tour.generateDescription: Create images, videos, or audio with local or cloud workflows.
tour.generate1: Single mode is for one-off image, video, or audio jobs.
tour.generate2: Director mode walks through Setup, Script, Keyframes, and Videos.
tour.generate3: If a workflow is missing models or nodes, use Re-check before you queue anything.
tour.stockDescription: Search Pexels and import footage or stills directly into the current project.
tour.stock1: Best used when you need quick placeholder footage, inspiration, or background plates.
tour.stock2: Requires a Pexels API key in Settings.
tour.exportDescription: Render the current timeline to a deliverable file and manage the export queue.
tour.export1: Choose format, codec, render range, resolution, FPS, and audio settings.
tour.export2: Queue multiple exports if you want a few output variants.
tour.settingsDescription: Return here whenever the machine-specific setup changes.
tour.settings1: Projects folder, ComfyUI port, Comfy account API key, Pexels key, and new-project defaults all live here.
tour.settings2: If something works on one machine and not another, this is the first place to compare.

gettingStarted.footer: This in-app guide covers the essentials. See the videos for detailed editing and prompting techniques.
